title: Check yourself: The four stages and the price of a team

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Cobalt Logistics has three proposals for a returns-handling service. One has no way to learn from wrong answers, one is a workflow and one is a team of agents. A board member wants the cheapest. What should the architect do first?

options.text: Reject the cheapest design if the board has not yet seen its performance figures on live data
options.says: Ruled out because rejection follows a missing stage, not missing live figures: "a design with a missing stage or an unapproved write is rejected first".

options.text: Judge all of them on the same four stages and drop any that lacks one
options.says: A review applies the same questions to every design, and the missing stage is the first finding.

options.text: Ask each team to run its design on a hundred real returns and compare the token bills
options.says: Ruled out because price is compared only "among those that pass the review".

options.text: Choose the workflow because workflows cost less than an agent on this workload
options.says: Ruled out because the page prices a workflow at "one chat per step", so a long workflow can cost more than the rung above it.

questions.stem: Scenario: Heron Analytics' task splits into six independent parts, and one context could not hold all the reading, but its value is about the cost of a single chat. What does the rule conclude?

options.text: Use the team, since independence and volume are the hard conditions and value follows
options.says: Ruled out because "a team that fails the third loses money on every run".

options.text: Use the team, since value can be raised later by adding more agents to it
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "it needs independence, volume and value together", and adding agents raises cost, not value.

options.text: Neither level of autonomy pays, so leave it on a plain call or drop it
options.says: Two of the three conditions hold and the third fails, so no autonomous rung pays.

options.text: Use one agent, since a team needs only independence among the parts
options.says: Ruled out because for this task "its value is below what even one agent costs".
